subject: Re: Deltasight migration — final capacity validation & cutover choreography
messages:

Subject: Deltasight hosted->dedicated timeline and final sizing questions

Rishi / Monica —

Thanks for the call this morning. We're excited to move from hosted to a dedicated pool but need to lock the final sizing and the migration window. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Target steady-state throughput: ~120 qps (avg request size ~350 tokens, 95th token length ~600)
- Model profile: llama-3-70b (quantized int8), heavy long-context use, KV cache expected to grow up to ~8GB per session for our largest flows
- Desired p99 generation latency: <= 400ms for 1–4 token responses, <= 1.2s for longer generations

Can you confirm the GPU count / instance types you recommend for a dedicated pool that meets the above with 20% headroom for bursts? Also need the proposed cutover blackout window (our ops prefers a weeknight) and rollback criteria.

Appreciate a short mutual action plan we can put in procurement.

—Ava
Ava Chambers
Head of Product, Deltasight
ava.chambers@deltasight.com

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deltasight hosted->dedicated timeline and final sizing questions

Ava —

Thanks — this is actionable. High-level answers below; Monica/Karthik/Ben are looped for the technical runbook and cutover window. I'll draft an MAP we can attach to the SOW. Quick summary: 

- Initial dedicated fleet recommendation: 6x A800-class GPUs (or equivalent A100 80G if preferred) with 2 extra warm standby GPUs for burst/failover (so 8 total reserved). This sizing targets ~120 qps for your model profile with quantized int8 and 20% headroom.
- Throughput assumptions: batching at 8–12 tokens average, continuous KV-prefetch for sticky sessions; expect 60–70 tokens/s per GPU for heavy long-context loads in our tests.
- Latency: Achievable p99 <= 400ms on short responses with continuous batching and prefix caching; longer generations vary with sampling.
- Rollback criteria: sustained p95 latency > 1.5s for 15 minutes OR error rate > 0.8% for 5 minutes after cutover.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Karthik to run a 2-hour synthetic stress run this week using your sample prompt set (+2x traffic) and share telemetry.
2) Monica to produce a cutover runbook (timings, DNS switching, traffic quiesce, canary traffic cadence).
3) Ben to propose exact maintenance window options (Thu night, Fri night, Sun night).
4) I'll place the MAP into the SOW for procurement to sign.

I'll attach a strawman MAP and the proposed cutover checklist once Ben/Karthik confirm windows.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Deltasight hosted->dedicated timeline and final sizing questions

Ava / team —

Thanks for the numbers, those help. A few pragmatic notes for the runbook: 

- Canary plan: 2 progressive canaries at 5% and 25% traffic for 30 minutes each with metric gates (latency, error rate, token cost). If gates pass, advance to full traffic in a rolling 15-minute ramp.
- Cache warm strategy: pre-populate top-500 prompt prefixes using a KV-restore snapshot before cutover window start; this reduces first-minute p99 spikes.
- Data plane fallback: keep hosted API routing for 48 hours post-cutover as an emergency fallback (automated traffic split rollback).

I'll produce the cutover runbook spreadsheet and share. For the SOW/MAP, please include: acceptance test (synthetic traffic profile + live QA sample), SLA target p99 numbers for 7-day monitoring, and credit/rollback compensation clauses.

—Monica
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deltasight hosted->dedicated timeline and final sizing questions

Ava / all —

I've scheduled a synthetic load test for Wed 25 Nov at 02:00 UTC using the Deltasight prompt set; test details below: 

- Load profile: 2-hour run, steady 150 qps (20% over target) with 10 minute ramp-up and 10 minute cool-down. Mixed distribution: 60% short responses (<100 tokens), 40% long-context (>400 tokens).
- Environment: dedicated emulation on 6x A800s + 2 warm spares (8 GPUs total) with int8 quantization, continuous batching=8, KV cache limit to 8GB/session for large flows.
- Telemetry to capture: token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, memory pressure, batch sizes, kernel fallback events, error codes.
- Acceptance gates: p99 short-response <= 450ms, p99 long-response <= 1.3s, error rate < 0.5%.

I'll upload the test logs to SUP-8421 and share summary by EOD. If gates pass, we propose cutover window options: Thu 26 Nov 02:00-06:00 UTC (Thu night PT), or Sun 29 Nov 03:00-07:00 UTC. Ben — can you confirm on-call and runbook handoffs for those windows?

Thanks,
Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Confirming on-call coverage and runbook ownership: 

- On-call: Myself + 2x infra engineers on standby for the cutover windows (Thu 26 Nov 02:00-06:00 UTC OR Sun 29 Nov 03:00-07:00 UTC). We'll be in the escalation channel.
- DNS change plan: traffic will be shifted via our routing layer (canary -> ramp -> full) with a 5-minute sticky session drain per backend.
- Rollback steps: revert routing to hosted API, redeploy a hot-failover k8s job to reclaim sessions, and kick off cache restore on hosted side if required. Estimated rollback recovery time: ~12 minutes median.

Attachments: initial cutover_runbook (spreadsheet) attached for review. Please flag any gaps by EOD Wed.

—Ben
